- Pricing models supported: flat fee, negotiated fee based on promoter and event details
- Pricing model details: Fee is negotiated depending on promoter, location, and event length. We will charge as much as we can when possible and adjust rates to win the job. Never less than £35k for a month unless it's a multi-month deal.
- Minimum run length: 1
- Minimum run length details: No minimum event length - anything if the price is right, but normally minimum is one day
- Sessions per day: Flexible; typically hourly sessions.
- Session length: 1 hour
- Turnaround time: No separate turnaround/break; any reset is built into session timing.
- Indoor arena template: No difference in approach; Monster operates the same in all venue types. Exact operations are up to the promoter with Event Manager's guidance.
- Outdoor park template: No difference in approach; Monster operates the same in all venue types. Exact operations are up to the promoter with Event Manager's guidance.
- Payment terms: deposit 50, due upon signing the contract, balance other 50% before unpacking on arrival; some negotiation and flexibility is possible
- Accepted methods: bank transfer
- Territory rules: Territory or date range exclusivity is available for promoters depending on their requirements.
- Discounting policy: Negotiable; discounting is possible depending on context and promoter. | approved by All discounts are approved directly by me. Negotiations are handled case by case with the promoter.
- Cancellation / reschedule terms: Refunds are not provided except under extraordinary circumstances, which would be considered on a negotiated basis.

- Hard NO conditions:
- ceiling height under 6m
- insufficient ground space for inflatable
- ground not flat or clear of sharp objects or hazards
- ceiling height under 6m (Monster), under 9m (Mega Bounce House)
- Hard NO details: Minimum 6m ceiling clearance for Monster and 9m for Mega Bounce House and enough ground space to fit the inflatable are required. The ground must be flat and clear of sharp objects or anything that could damage the inflatable. As long as the inflatable can be staked or bolted, most surfaces are suitable.
- Monster footprint: inflatable-only 35 m wide by 90 m long, full festival Includes our touring inflatables: giant tentacles, sofa, sign, unicorn. Additional 'side dressing' is up to the promoter, but our provided elements ensure a minimum lively appearance.
- Mega Bounce House footprint: Minimum floor space for Mega Bounce House: 75m x 60m. Ceiling height minimum 9m.
- Access requirements: truck access 40-ft lorry access required, load-in route Forklift and pallet jack needed for load-in, door sizes Assessed case by case
- Ground and anchoring: Concrete weights can be used for anchoring if required, but this is costly and more complicated.
- Weather thresholds: wind Shutdown thresholds and procedures follow UK regulations for inflatables: event must pause or shut down if wind speed exceeds 24 mph (38 kph) or gusts exceed manufacturer recommendations., rain Operations paused or managed according to manufacturer and regulatory guidance in severe rain or if water accumulation is unsafe., heat Extreme heat: Event Manager assesses safety. Pause or shut down if crew/judgement determines heat is hazardous to staff or guests.

- Baseline Monster staffing: One Event Manager (provided by us), 10 local crew for setup/packdown (provided by promoter), and event staff: minimum of 7 to maximum of 13 depending on event scale (provided by promoter).
- Baseline Mega Bounce House staffing: One Event Manager (provided by us), 10 local crew for setup/packdown (provided by promoter), and event staff: minimum of 7 to maximum of 13 depending on event scale (provided by promoter).
- Role reasons: Event Manager oversees, 10 local crew (minimum) for setup/packdown, and 7–13 event staff (depending on event scale) operate inflatable and support event operations.
- Can scale down: false
- Minimum viable staffing: 10
- Training: Our Event Manager trains the local crew. / 1 to 2 hours
- Failure modes:
- Crew are late, do not turn up, are not strong, or are unprofessional

- Power plan: All power contingencies, including provision of backup generator, are promoter's responsibility and risk. We recommend a backup generator if main power is from a generator.
- Lighting / sound / staging: Always up to promoter unless we are handling full event production.
- Bar & food: All catering and bar setups outside the UK are strictly the promoter's responsibility; no involvement from us. For UK gigs, we only provide bar/food if we're running the setup ourselves—otherwise, promoter handles everything including licensing.
- Queueing & crowd flow: Groups of 4–6 are admitted to the Monster at a time, adjusted based on inflatable size and group numbers. A staff member at the entrance gives a safety talk and warm-up to each group before entry. As a group passes a certain section, the next group is allowed through, creating a flow of approximately one group every 30 seconds. Coordination is managed by the staff at the front and on the Monster, using cues to control entry.
- On-site comms: One radio with earpiece is required for each team member and all on-site staff, including medics and security. radios, All radios must have an earpiece. in-ear

- Included marketing support: Full marketing kit provided: all video and photo collateral, video edits, source files, InDesign templates, press release templates, and access to marketing team for questions.
- Not included: We provide all assets, collateral, and templates, but the promoter is responsible for executing all marketing activity. We can advise, suggest, and approve as needed, but the work is entirely promoter-driven.
- Benchmarks: No paid social CPA data tracked; responsibility for paid social is entirely on the promoter.
- Press & PR: Press release templates provided
- Objection handling:
- TBD

- Insurance: Naming us as a nominated party is sufficient.
- Damage / liability: Usual wear and tear is covered by us. No history of billing promoters for damages.
- Permits / licensing: All local/regional event permits and compliance are the promoter's responsibility. Safety certification requirements for each market should be discussed.
- Brand claims / restrictions: No restrictions; promoters can use any wording or marketing claims they prefer.

- Lead qualification questions:
- What are the dates for your proposed event?
- Where is the event located?
- What is the nature and type of event?
- Do you have sufficient available space for the inflatable? (Monster requires a minimum of 35m x 90m. Mega Bounce House requires a minimum of 75m x 60m and 9m ceiling height.)
- Disqualification rules:
- IF Lead or promoter is disqualified if unable or unwilling to pay the 50% (or agreed) non-refundable upfront deposit unless mutual agreement for refund is reached.
- IF Event is disqualified if it is a kid's birthday party, charity event, or school event without sufficient budget.
- Product matching logic:
- All leads come to me for direct review and product matching; no fully automated product matching logic.
- Escalation triggers:
- Flag and escalate leads identified as repeat time wasters.

This file extracts only the useful sales, positioning, proof, and visual-context information from the two promoter decks:

- `MONSTER MASTER PRES 2025_SUPERSIZE (1).pdf`
- `BOUNCE NATION PRODUCT DECK (1).pdf`

It is designed to sit alongside `full-checklist.md`, not replace it.

`full-checklist.md` remains the operational and commercial source of truth for pricing, payment terms, included services, promoter responsibilities, space/height qualification, staffing reality, power responsibility, weather rules, legal edge cases, and CRM qualification rules.

Use this addendum for natural-language product understanding, sales copy, lead-context enrichment, marketing angles, and product-positioning answers. Do not use it to override the checklist.

---

When answering questions, the copilot should apply this priority order:

1. `full-checklist.md` is authoritative for anything operational, contractual, commercial, legal, staffing, venue-fit, delivery, qualification, or promoter-responsibility related.
2. This addendum is authoritative only for deck-derived sales positioning, product story, audience appeal, visual descriptions, proof points, historical examples, and marketing language.
3. The older file `knoledge-base.md.txt` should be treated as deprecated unless its content is also present in either `full-checklist.md` or this addendum.
4. If a deck claim conflicts with the checklist, the copilot must follow the checklist and, where useful, mention that the deck contains older or promoter-facing wording that should be verified before quoting externally.
5. Do not invent pricing, availability, local compliance rules, insurance requirements, technical drawings, or final site-plan approval. Escalate those to Nick / the event manager.

The Monster is positioned as the world's biggest inflatable party and the world's largest inflatable obstacle-course experience. The promoter deck frames it as a high-energy, festival-style attraction built around adult nostalgia, group fun, music, spectacle, and social sharing.

The key emotional hook is: adults get to relive the feeling of 1990s game shows, obstacle-course TV, and childhood inflatable fun in a large-scale event format.

Useful sales-language ideas:

- World's biggest inflatable party.
- Ultimate party playground.
- 300 metres of bouncy mayhem.
- A giant 1990s game-show fantasy brought to life.
- A festival-style inflatable experience with music, food, bars, lighting, visuals, and social-photo moments.
- A headline attraction that can be adapted for adults, families, kids, corporate groups, and competitive sessions.

The deck describes a full Monster event as more than the inflatable course alone. The wider experience can include:

- A 300-metre inflatable obstacle course.
- 42 obstacles.
- Live DJs.
- Giant flamingo and unicorn ball pits.
- Giant inflatable set dressing.
- Street food.
- Bars.
- Live action cameras on a big screen.
- High-end sound, lighting, and special effects.
- Start and finish moments designed for photos and group celebration.

For copilot responses, describe this as an event concept that can be scaled up or down depending on what the promoter is responsible for providing. The checklist makes clear that production elements such as bar, food, lighting, sound, staging, and extra event production are not automatically included unless agreed.

The Monster deck gives these proof points:

- First launched in London in 2017.
- First major event was at Alexandra Palace.
- Sold 20,000 tickets within four weeks for the first event.
- Has toured 35 cities.
- Has operated in 9 countries.
- Has sold more than 450,000 tickets.
- Has operated across the UK, Europe, the Middle East, the USA, and Canada.
- Example deck locations include Miami Beach 2023, Abu Dhabi New Year's Day 2021, and Victoria, Canada 2023.

Use these as credibility points when a lead asks whether the attraction is proven, scalable, or internationally tourable.

The Monster deck presents the product as versatile across:

- Sports arenas.
- Indoor arenas.
- Conference centres.
- Parks.
- Beaches.
- Resort-style outdoor spaces.

The visual site-plan pages show the Monster as a flexible outdoor festival layout with a main arena, stage zone, entrance/exit area, bars, food trucks, queueing, seating, furniture, fencing, and branded dressing. These are useful for helping promoters imagine the event, but they should not be treated as an included production package.

The deck says the Monster does not always need to be an adult party format. It can also be positioned for:

- Team-building.
- Sport and fun-fitness concepts.
- Parent-and-kids events.
- Dedicated kids-only events.
- Family fun days.
- Competition formats.
- Corporate events.
- Sports clubs and active social groups.

This is useful for lead matching. The Monster is strongest when a promoter wants a ticketable, scheduled, high-energy experience with clear group appeal.

The deck gives these audience claims:

- 68% female.
- 75% aged 20-35.
- 25% aged 36-44.
- Audience described as experience seekers.
- Broad appeal includes pleasure seekers, fitness fans, groups, hen parties, bachelor parties, birthday parties, corporate groups, team-building groups, families, competitors, and sports clubs.
- The event can also work for kids and families where the format is appropriate.

Use this for sales positioning and audience fit. Do not use it as a guarantee of local attendance demographics.

The deck includes press and fan quotes. Use these carefully as marketing flavour rather than operational facts.

Press-style language shown in the deck includes:

- Time Out: relive every 90s game-show fantasy.
- Evening Standard: tremendous fun.
- The Independent: every childhood game show crammed into one long bouncy dream.
- London in Stereo: if you get no joy from the Monster, you're an animal.

Fan-comment themes include:

- Non-stop laughs.
- Amazing tunes.
- Crazy fun and totally different.
- Crying with laughter.
- Can we go again?
- Absolutely incredible.

The copilot can use these themes to help draft promotional copy, but should avoid overusing exact quotes unless the user specifically asks for deck-style marketing language.

The deck visuals emphasize:

- Big, colourful inflatable structures.
- A giant monster-mouth entrance.
- Large slides and obstacle sections.
- Bright tropical/set-dressing elements.
- Party lighting and festival energy.
- Start/finish signage.
- Social-media-friendly photo moments.
- Outdoor festival layouts with food, drink, stage, seating, and queue control.

This context helps the copilot describe the product in richer natural language when responding to leads.

The Mega Bounce House is positioned as the world's biggest bounce house and a large-scale standalone destination attraction. The deck frames it as colourful, family-friendly, visually massive, and easy for guests to understand immediately.

Useful sales-language ideas:

- The world's biggest bounce house.
- 27,000 square feet of bouncy madness.
- A destination attraction, not just a side activity.
- A visual landmark that draws attention from a distance.
- A high-energy, high-capacity inflatable experience for kids, adults, and families.
- Ideal for creating social-media moments and drawing large crowds.

The deck describes Mega Bounce House as a vast inflatable environment with:

- Oversized characters.
- Large architectural inflatable elements.
- Sports zones.
- Obstacle-course style areas.
- Slides.
- Open bounce areas.
- Colourful side dressing.
- Tall walls and oversized visual features.

The experience is free-flowing rather than race-based. It is easy for mixed-age audiences to understand and is especially strong for daytime, family, and high-footfall public events.

Mega Bounce House is best positioned for:

- Family-focused festivals.
- City and council events.
- Public-space activations.
- High-footfall destination attractions.
- Daytime programming.
- Events where the promoter wants visual impact with less need for a competitive or timed race concept.

The deck shows both children and adults using the attraction, so the copilot should not describe it as kids-only. It is family-friendly and intergenerational.

The deck gives these sales facts:

- 27,000 square feet.
- Walls over 26 feet high.
- Capacity of 250 people at one time.
- Recommended minimum experience duration of 30 minutes.

Use these for sales positioning, but do not use deck operational specs to override checklist qualification requirements.

The Mega Bounce House deck visuals emphasize:

- Large purple, teal, pink, orange, and yellow inflatable structures.
- A giant central character/mascot feature.
- Slides, climbing points, balance elements, sports-style play zones, and obstacle features.
- Inflatable palm-tree dressing and large playful architectural forms.
- A bright family-friendly visual identity.
- Strong aerial and photo-friendly impact.

This context helps the copilot describe Mega Bounce House as colourful, playful, and highly visible.

Answer as a sales description first, then qualify operational details from the checklist.

Recommended answer style:

The Monster is a large-scale inflatable obstacle-course and party experience. It is built around a 300-metre course with 42 obstacles and can be packaged as a festival-style attraction with music, food, bars, lighting, branding, and social-photo moments. It is especially strong for ticketed sessions, adult nostalgia, team-building, competitive formats, and high-energy group events. Final venue fit, staffing, production responsibilities, and pricing should be checked against the operational checklist and confirmed by Nick/event management.

Answer as a destination attraction first, then qualify operational details from the checklist.

Recommended answer style:

Mega Bounce House is a huge, colourful touring bounce-house attraction designed as a standalone destination for families, kids, adults, and high-footfall public events. It is promoted as 27,000 square feet, with oversized characters, slides, sports zones, obstacle-style areas, and open bounce spaces. It works best when the promoter wants a simple, highly visual, free-flowing attraction rather than a timed obstacle-course experience. Final space, height, staffing, power, and logistics should be checked against the operational checklist.

The copilot should say that the decks show examples of what a larger event environment can look like, including stage, food trucks, bars, fencing, seating, entrance/exit arches, and lighting. These elements help sell the vision but are not automatically included. The checklist says the promoter is responsible for production unless a full event-production package is separately agreed.

Use the checklist version. Do not copy old deck numbers into qualification answers if the checklist gives a stricter or newer requirement.

The following deck or old-KB details overlap with, or conflict with, `full-checklist.md`. The copilot should not treat them as primary qualification facts.

- The Mega Bounce House deck says minimum space is 50m x 50m. The checklist says minimum floor space is 75m x 60m and ceiling height minimum is 9m. Use the checklist.
- The deck says minimum 6 event staff. The checklist says event staffing is typically 7-13 plus setup/packdown crew, provided by the promoter. Use the checklist.
- The deck says setup is 8 hours, packdown is 6 hours, with 14 crew. The checklist gives the current staffing reality and promoter responsibilities. Use the checklist for qualification and delivery planning.
- The old KB repeats the deck's 50m x 50m space and 6-staff figures. Treat these as deprecated.

- The Monster deck says ideal space is 90m x 50m with 7m height clearance, and 70m x 35m for the inflatable only. The checklist says Monster requires minimum 35m x 90m and minimum 6m ceiling clearance. Use the checklist for qualification.
- The deck says The Monster supplies 1 technician and 1 tour/staffing manager. The checklist says one Event Manager is provided. Use the checklist unless Nick confirms otherwise for a particular deal.
- The deck production rider lists many event elements such as stage, sound, lighting, LED screen, bars, food trucks, cloakroom, barriers, fencing, paramedics, security, radios, and optional smoke/haze. The checklist says these are promoter responsibilities unless full event production is agreed. Do not present them as included.
- The old KB repeats several deck technical specs and should not be used as the operational source of truth.

Do not duplicate commercial terms, payment terms, cancellation policy, insurance, permits, promoter responsibilities, or CRM qualification rules from the checklist into this addendum. Those belong only in `full-checklist.md`.

Use this structure for the product copilot:

1. `full-checklist.md` - unchanged, authoritative operational/commercial checklist from Nick.
2. `product-decks-rag-addendum.md` - this file, for deck-derived positioning, proof, audience, formats, and visual description.
3. `knoledge-base.md.txt` - archive/deprecate. Do not include it in active RAG unless it is rewritten to remove conflicts and duplication.

This avoids the biggest risk: the copilot answering with old deck specs when Nick's checklist contains newer, stricter, or more practical delivery rules.
